summary: Opaque white outer coat of the globe; yellows slightly with age.

radius.note: Radius of the scleral sphere used to shape the visible globe.

limbal_zone_width.note: Width of the translucent grey-blue corneoscleral transition; the cornea-sclera join is a smooth groove this wide.

overlap_superior.note: How far the sclera overlaps the cornea at 12 o'clock, making the visible front an oval (confidence low; Wolff's Anatomy 8th ed., 11.7 x 10.6 front; hidden under the lid in this subject).

overlap_inferior.note: How far the sclera overlaps the cornea at 6 o'clock (confidence low; source.jpg shows about 0.2; the slit-lamp reference shows about 0.7).

translucent_width_horizontal.note: 10-90% width of the translucent limbal band at 3 and 9 o'clock (confidence low; render-measured 0.53-0.59 nasal in source.jpg, 0.47-0.57 in the user reference).

translucent_width_vertical.note: 10-90% width of the translucent limbal band at 12 and 6 o'clock (confidence low; Hogan 1971: limbus wider vertically, about 1.5-2 mm against about 1 mm horizontally).

base_colour.note: Linear albedo; sRGB #dde7ec sampled from the clean temporal sclera of assets/exterior/source.jpg (render calibration).

provenance.source: Atchison & Smith (2000), ch. 2 (radius); Olsen et al., Am J Ophthalmol 125:237 (1998) (thickness); Bron, Tripathi & Tripathi, Wolff's Anatomy of the Eye and Orbit, 8th ed. (limbal zone, overlap); Hogan, Alvarado & Weddell, Histology of the Human Eye (1971) (vertical band); overlap and band widths: render calibration on assets/exterior/source.jpg and assets/refs/iris/gen-brown-01.png, see docs/realism/L5-cornea-tear.md; colour: render calibration from source.jpg
